issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' (and specify a static final Stock stock in SealSaloon). However, the provided template and the solution implement a class named 'Inventory' that exposes the same methods (add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock). Additionally, src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java in the repository is empty. This naming mismatch (problem text/UML: 'Stock' vs code: 'Inventory') will confuse students about which class to use or modify and may lead to incorrect type usage when they implement SealSaloon (the text asks for a Stock-typed field but only Inventory is provided).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across the problem text, template, and solution. Either (A) rename the provided Inventory class (and its usages) to Stock and remove or implement the empty Stock.java file, or (B) update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory (change examples and the SealSaloon stock field/type to Inventory). Ensure the chosen name is used consistently in the template, solution, and tests so students are not required to reconcile mismatched names.
